title: Flowing Current and Idle Pause
description: A design lab for two p5.js showcase techniques: evenly spaced dots flow along a battery-and-lamp loop defined by corner points (offset modulo spacing, lerp along each segment, hidden inside the lamp), and pause-when-idle stops the animation's progress when the pointer leaves, as shown by a live animation step counter.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: p5.js
Animation Design
Flowing Current Animation
Pause-When-Idle
publisher: MicroSims 2.0: Generating, Instrumenting and Evaluating Interactive Learning Objects with AI

educational.topic: Flowing current animation and pause-when-idle in p5.js MicroSims
learningObjectives: The learner will design a flowing-current animation by choosing path, spacing, and speed, and will decide whether pause-when-idle should be on, by observing the effect on the animation and on a live step counter.
prerequisites: Flowing Current Animation and Pause-When-Idle Animation sections (Chapter 6)
The animation loop and frame rate (Chapter 6)

accessibility.notes: No flashing; a tap sets the pointer-over flag on touch screens

equations: first dot at flowOffset mod spacing, then every spacing pixels along the path
dot position = lerp(corner i, corner i+1, t) inside the segment containing its distance
advancing = running AND (pause-when-idle off OR pointer over the sim)
assumptions: Speed is per frame, so the real speed follows the frame rate (lap time shown at 60 fps)
limitations: The dots visualize conventional current; they are not a model of electron speed

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Design by iteration with a live measurement (step counter and lap time)
keyQuestions: Which spacing and speed make the direction of flow obvious without blur?
What exactly stops when the pointer leaves, and what keeps running?
commonMisconceptions: The dot speed represents the speed of electrons
assessmentOpportunities: A justified design choice of spacing, speed and direction
A written decision on pause-when-idle for a given page
